clock_dir_to: The backward clock reading is obligatorily marked, and marked at the END of
the phrase: 세 시 십 분 전 is ten minutes BEFORE three, 02:50.  Because the
marker is required and final, the forward and backward readings never
collide and neither has to be guessed.  Elon.io, Korean grammar, "Half, To,
clock_fraction_30: 반 is "half", and on a clock it stands in for 삼십 분: it counts FORWARD
from the hour just named, so 두 시 반 is 2:30.  Elon.io, Korean grammar,
"Half, To, and Past: 반, 전, 후"; the same forward reading appears in Korean
Study Junkie, "Telling Time in Korean", with 열두시반 for 12:30.

marker_past: Unicode CLDR 47, cldr-json cldr-dates-full/main/ko/dateFields.json.  The "N units ago" pattern ends in 전.
전 also means "before" on a clock face, where it turns a minute count into
minutes BEFORE the hour just named (세 시 십 분 전 is ten to three).  The
two readings never collide, because the clock one is licensed by a named
hour standing in front of it and this one is not.

unit1_day: Korean marks no number on a noun, so the counted and uncounted forms of
a unit are one and the same word.  Listed here as well so the engine reads
this locale as having no plural unit surfaces at all.

unit_day: Unicode CLDR 47, cldr-json cldr-dates-full/main/ko/dateFields.json.  "{0}일 전" / "{0}일 후".
일 also marks the day of the month (3월 15일) and is the Sino numeral one.
The readings are told apart by position, never by the string: the day
marker follows a day number inside a date, the duration unit carries its
own count and a direction word.
unit_hour: Unicode CLDR 47, cldr-json cldr-dates-full/main/ko/dateFields.json.  "{0}시간 전" / "{0}시간 후".
시간 counts hours; 시 names the hour of the clock and is not a duration.
unit_minute: Unicode CLDR 47, cldr-json cldr-dates-full/main/ko/dateFields.json.  "{0}분 전" / "{0}분 후".
unit_month: Unicode CLDR 47, cldr-json cldr-dates-full/main/ko/dateFields.json.  The COUNTED month is 개월 -- "{0}개월 전" --
and not the calendar label 월, which numbers the months of the year (3월 is
March).  The two are grammatical in the same position and mean different
things, so only the counter ships here; 월 stays a month name.
달 is the native month noun, the unit of 지난달 / 이번 달 / 다음 달.
unit_second: Unicode CLDR 47, cldr-json cldr-dates-full/main/ko/dateFields.json.  "{0}초 전" / "{0}초 후".
unit_week: Unicode CLDR 47, cldr-json cldr-dates-full/main/ko/dateFields.json.  "{0}주 전" / "{0}주 후".
주일 is the fuller form of the same noun (일주일 is one week).
unit_year: Unicode CLDR 47, cldr-json cldr-dates-full/main/ko/dateFields.json.  "{0}년 전" / "{0}년 후".
해 is the native word for the year, the unit the relative-period forms
작년 / 올해 / 내년 name (dateFields year relative-type -1/0/1).
weekday_0: The abbreviated forms CLDR also carries are single syllables (일 월 화 수
목 금 토) and each is an ordinary word in its own right -- 일 is the day,
the numeral one and Sunday at once, 월 is the month and Monday, 수 is a
number and water, 금 is gold.  Nothing inside the phrase tells the readings
apart; only a calendar grid does, and a grid is not prose.  They are
therefore not shipped, and a bare abbreviation names no weekday here.
